text:
oncall-bot: PAGER — hosted-api (canary) 2a/2b experiencing elevated 500s, 12% error rate over 5m. Paging oncall team. Incident ID: INC-2026-17980

sam: I'm oncall. looking. pulling logs + traces now.

sam: quick check — canary rollout started 03:10 UTC (about 6m ago). I see spikes exactly after pods with image tag release-2026.03.15 hit. 500s show upstream errors: KMS permission denied when fetching model encryption key.
jess: @sam hmm. we rotated keys last night as part of ops-maint. @maria did the deploy pick up new key name or a new env var?
maria: yes — release included MODEL_KMS_KEY=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ml/cryptoKeys/redwood-key-v2. Can confirm canary containers got that env var. It was tested in staging with patched IAM.
sam: can you paste the env from a failing pod?
maria: sure — exec into canary pod and env grep:
```
kubectl exec -it hosted-api-canary-1 -- printenv | grep MODEL_KMS_KEY
MODEL_KMS_KEY=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ml/cryptoKeys/redwood-key-v2
```

sam: logs show 403 from Cloud KMS: 
```
Error: PermissionDenied: cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt for resource projects/redwood/.../cryptoKeys/redwood-key-v2
stack: runtime/kms_client.go:112
```

jess: that implies the service account used by canary doesn't have `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt` on the v2 key. Did the IAM migration apply to canary nodes?
maria: IAM terraform applied only to prod control-plane role, looks like canary SA binding was missed. I pushed the TF change but maybe it didn't land before canary pods spun up.

olivia: Customer-facing side: we have ~10 active customers hitting canary endpoints. Support is starting to see request failures. Noticed spikes in error budgets on a few premium routes.

sam: mitigation options: 1) quickly add IAM binding to grant canary SA useToDecrypt on v2 key, 2) toggle feature flag to point canary to old key (redwood-key-v1), or 3) rollback canary to previous image. Fastest safe option?
jess: toggle feature flag sounds fastest if we have a kill-switch on routing. But feature flag touches routing config — risk of partial state. IAM binding is infra change — might take a couple min to propagate. Rollback is straightforward via deployment rollback.
maria: I can rollback the canary within 1 minute using our release job. I'll do a canary-only rollback (no prod). Rolling back now to image release-2026.03.08.

maria: `/release rollback hosted-api --to-tag=release-2026.03.08 --target=canary`

oncall-bot: Deploy job started by maria at 1798005840

sam: monitoring logs and error rate. If rollback doesn't cut it, we'll add IAM binding as fallback.

security-bot: SECURITY ALERT: The new key redwood-key-v2 exists in KMS. Last rotation: 2026-03-15T01:20Z. IAM policy change required: grant `serviceAccount:canary-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` the roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter role.

kevin: I'm on sec. adding binding via emergency terraform apply now. Will scope to canary SA and only decrypter permission.

kevin: running: `terraform apply -target=google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding.redwood_key_v2_canary`
kevin: apply done in 45s. Policy updated.
sam: error rate dropped from 12% -> 2% after rollback started. Looks promising.

maria: canary pods are now back to release-2026.03.08. Confirming env still points to v2 key? should be old image that uses v1, yes.

jess: good catch. We need to check how TF churn hit control-plane but not canary SA binding. Postmortem item.
sam: timeline note: 03:10 canary rollout with v2 key env. 03:12 500s spike detected. 03:13 page fired. 03:15 rollback started. 03:18 rollback completed. 03:20 error rate returned to baseline.

olivia: telling support to mark impacted customers (IDs: C-448, C-1129) — they saw failed requests during window 03:12–03:20. We'll draft notification.

maria: follow-up actions I'm owning: 1) add canary SA binding to infra terraform and run plan checks as part of release pipeline; 2) add pre-flight check that compares MODEL_KMS_KEY env with IAM policies before rollout; 3) add explicit canary IAM sync step.
jess: ops: add a `check-kms-access` job to the release pipeline that runs: 
```
python tools/check_kms_access.py --sa canary-sa --key projects/.../redwood-key-v2
```
and fail rollout if 403.

kevin: security will review rotation runbooks to ensure bindings propagate. Also will create an alert for `KMS:access_denied` in canary namespace that pages infra-oncall.

sam: incident severity? Customer impact limited (canary) but some customers hit canary routes and saw failures. I'd mark Sev2 and logged.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-17980 marked RESOLVED by sam at 1798006240 (mitigated: canary rollback + IAM patch).

sam: closing notes: immediate mitigation = rollback to previous image. IAM patch applied as belt-and-suspenders. Postmortem: ensure release pipeline includes IAM preflight and feature-flag kill-switch baked into canary route config.

olivia: I'll send a brief status to customers and create a support ticket summary.

jess: thanks everyone. I'll add postmortem doc and link after investigation.

maria: tagging action items in the release epic.

kevin: reopening if we see regression. Otherwise good to close. :white_check_mark:
